facts.text: Hotel Eden first opened in 1889.
facts.excerpt: First opened in 1889, Hotel Eden is infused with authentic Roman spirit and alive with the stories of a legendary city.

facts.text: Hotel Eden is at Via Ludovisi 49 in Rome.
facts.excerpt: Hotel Eden is at Via Ludovisi 49, 00187 Rome, perfectly positioned in the heart of the city.

facts.text: The Spanish Steps are a 5-minute walk from the hotel.
facts.excerpt: Yes, the legendary Spanish Steps are just a 5-minute walk away.

facts.text: La Terrazza is the hotel's one-Michelin-starred fine dining restaurant.
facts.excerpt: La Terrazza, Hotel Eden, Rome, is our one-Michelin starred fine dining restaurant.

facts.text: La Terrazza is located on the top floor with views over Rome.
facts.excerpt: Located on the top floor, it offers guests mesmerising views over Rome alongside a remarkable Michelin-starred dining experience.

facts.text: Michelin-starred chef Salvatore Bianco leads the cooking at La Terrazza.
facts.excerpt: Michelin-starred chef Salvatore Bianco brings artistic passion to La Terrazza, alongside a dedication to the finest ingredients

facts.text: La Terrazza serves dinner only and is closed on Sunday and Monday.
facts.excerpt: La Terrazza serves dinner only and is closed on Sunday and Monday.

facts.text: La Terrazza has short seasonal closures in January and August each year.
facts.excerpt: Yes, La Terrazza has short seasonal closures in January and August each year.

facts.text: Il Giardino Ristorante is a relaxed rooftop restaurant above the Spanish Steps, open daily.
facts.excerpt: Il Giardino Ristorante is our relaxed rooftop restaurant, soaring above Rome's Spanish Steps. It's open daily.

facts.text: La Terrazza, Il Giardino Ristorante and Il Giardino Bar are all on the hotel's rooftop.
facts.excerpt: Yes. La Terrazza, Il Giardino Ristorante and Il Giardino Bar are all located on our rooftop.

facts.text: Each month a guest chef creates a Sunday lunch menu with Salvatore Bianco for Il Giardino Ristorante in the Taste Society series.
facts.excerpt: Every month, a new guest chef dreams up a bespoke Sunday lunch menu for Il Giardino Ristorante. The ‘Taste Society’ series is a collaboration between Italy’s finest cooks and chef Salvatore Bianco

facts.text: Il Giardino Bar's views stretch from St Peter's to the Borghese gardens, from the Pincian Hill.
facts.excerpt: From our wonderful location on the Pincian Hill, all of Rome awaits your gaze. Your views stretch from the majesty of St Peter's to the stately Borghese gardens

facts.text: Il Giardino Bar has a vertical garden wall made from hundreds of handmade metal leaves.
facts.excerpt: our al fresco feel is brought to life by a ‘vertical garden’ wall. Crafted from hundreds of handmade metal leaves

facts.text: Il Giardino Bar's signature La Grande Bellezza cocktail is rose-hued.
facts.excerpt: Try the rose-hued La Grande Bellezza, which captures the warmth of a Roman sunset

facts.text: La Libreria is an elegant sitting room above the lobby with a secret bar behind mirrored doors.
facts.excerpt: A sitting room of unusual elegance positioned above the dynamic lobby, La Libreria is beautifully placed for popping in at any time of day.

facts.text: La Libreria's secret bar is behind mirrored doors.
facts.excerpt:
An opulent treat behind mirrored doors

Our secret bar hides precious bottles of renowned spirits, rare wines and more to be enjoyed.

facts.text: La Libreria hosts regular art workshops and exhibitions and a curated collection of books.
facts.excerpt: Immerse yourself in a world of art and culture at La Libreria, home to regular workshops, exhibitions and a curated collection of books.

facts.text: The spa gives each guest a dedicated suite with a private changing room and bathroom.
facts.excerpt: Each guest enjoys a dedicated suite—complete with a private changing room and bathroom—designed for ultimate comfort and seclusion.

facts.text: The spa uses Valmont and HöbePergh treatments.
facts.excerpt: Harnessing the power of Alpine herbs, our HöbePergh rituals deliver holistic wellness for the skin, body and mind.

facts.text: The fitness room is open 24 hours and is separate from the spa.
facts.excerpt: Yes, our fitness room is separate from the spa. It's open 24 hours a day.

facts.text: Hotel Eden does not have a pool.
facts.excerpt: Hotel Eden does not have a pool.

facts.text: Hotel Eden has no on-site parking but offers valet parking in a private garage nearby.
facts.excerpt: Hotel Eden does not have an on-site garage or parking lot but offers valet parking in a private garage nearby.

facts.text: The hotel welcomes up to two small dogs under 7 kg per room.
facts.excerpt: Yes, we welcome up to two small dogs (under 7 kg/15 lbs) per room

facts.text: Children over 6 are welcome at La Terrazza.
facts.excerpt: Children over 6 are welcome

facts.text: Children are always welcome at Il Giardino Ristorante, which has a children's menu.
facts.excerpt:
Children

Always welcome

facts.text: Prestige Rooms with View and Balcony are on the fifth floor with a private balcony.
facts.excerpt: Located on the fifth floor, these rooms radiate charm and comfort. Soak up their delights, then step out onto your very own balcony.

facts.text: The Ludovisi Suite is a two-bedroom suite.
facts.excerpt: Rome’s golden light floods through soaring windows in this luxurious two-bedroom suite.

facts.text: A complimentary extra bed is available in Junior Suites and above.
facts.excerpt: An extra bed is complimentary and can be accommodated in room categories from Junior Suites upwards.

facts.text: Eden Home is a bespoke porcelain tableware collection by Italian artist Coralla Maiuri.
facts.excerpt: A bespoke porcelain tableware collection from acclaimed Italian artist Coralla Maiuri

facts.text: Dorchester Collection acquired the Eden in 2013 and revamped it, adding a spa and a rooftop restaurant.
facts.excerpt: In 2013, The Dorchester Collection acquired the Eden and revamped it for the modern day, reducing the room count to 98, adding a spa and a rooftop restaurant

facts.text: Autographed photos of famous guests line the hotel stairwell.
facts.excerpt: Their autographed photos are crammed frame-to-frame in the hotel stairwell

facts.text: The hotel sits between the Villa Borghese gardens and Via Veneto.
facts.excerpt:
wedged between the
Villa Borghese
gardens and Rome’s upscale Via Veneto

facts.text: Guests can book a private Rebel and Rome tour of Caravaggio's haunts.
facts.excerpt: Guests can also book onto the “Rebel and Rome” trail, which takes you on a private tour of Caravaggio’s (lesser-known) haunts in the Eternal City.

facts.text: The Vatican is around a 30-minute drive away.
facts.excerpt: The Vatican is around a 30-minute drive away.

facts.text: Hotel calls La Libreria one of Rome's best-kept secrets.
facts.excerpt: Elegant and tucked away, it’s one of Rome’s best-kept secrets.

contradictions.note: official p5 says La Libreria is above the lobby; Conde Nast p10 says ground floor

in the ground floor La Libreria bar
